reflection.assumptions: Pandemic-related changes may have altered clinical work, service delivery, workload, safety concerns, and interactions with patients, requiring health workers to adapt to evolving demands and resource constraints. It is also important to consider how patient perceptions and experiences can vary significantly from healthcare provider perspectives. Additionally, I recognize that my focus on health worker experiences and adaptations may lead to an underappreciation of patient perspectives and the broader implications of healthcare policy decisions. I also see that the political context and healthcare management decisions can significantly shape the experiences of both patients and staff.
reflection.further_consideration: How do patient perceptions of safety and infection risk vary across different demographics, and how do these perceptions influence their interactions with the healthcare system? What role do institutional policies play in shaping both patient and staff experiences during health crises? How can I better integrate the broader operational context into my understanding of individual experiences?
reflection.reflexive_history:
1. [Phenomenon] Patient fear deters hospital visits
   [My code vs Peer code] Patient fear deters hospital visits vs Decrease in patient inflow due to fear of COVID-19
   [Evidence] 'But as soon as they sound the bell that there is a confirmed case in Sierra Leone, the patients in-flow dropped drastically.'
   [Interpretive difference] I emphasized the deterrent effect of patient fear specifically on hospital visits, while the peer highlighted the overall decrease in patient inflow.
   [Interpretive positioning] My perspective as a clinical nurse prioritizes the direct impact of fear on patient behavior, which I believe is crucial for understanding service delivery challenges.
   [Next-round adjustment] I will consider framing the phenomenon more broadly to include various aspects of patient inflow.

2. [Phenomenon] Fear of infection affects health worker behavior
   [My code vs Peer code] Fear of infection affects health worker behavior vs Fear of infection among healthcare workers
   [Evidence] 'It just made me to be very cautious and be with patients.'
   [Interpretive difference] I framed the code in terms of broader behavioral change, while the peer's code was more specific to the fear experienced by healthcare workers.
   [Interpretive positioning] My nursing background led me to generalize the implications of fear on health worker behavior, potentially overlooking the nuanced experiences described.
   [Next-round adjustment] I will strive to differentiate between the general impacts of fear and the specific fears faced by individual healthcare workers.

3. [Phenomenon] Implementation of triage system
   [My code vs Peer code] Implementation of triage system vs Implementation of infection control measures in the hospital
   [Evidence] 'But now it became compulsory as soon as you are at the hospital’s gate.'
   [Interpretive difference] I focused on the triage aspect as a direct response to patient management, while the peer framed it within a broader infection control context.
   [Interpretive positioning] My focus as a clinician prioritizes direct patient management strategies, which may not fully encompass the broader operational implications.
   [Next-round adjustment] I will consider how triage systems fit into larger infection control measures in future coding.

4. [Phenomenon] Changes in infection control measures
   [My code vs Peer code] Changes in infection control measures vs Management's response to prepare for COVID-19
   [Evidence] 'When I came here it was not….. people were bypassing the triage system.'
   [Interpretive difference] I focused on infection control measures as they pertain to individual practices, while the peer highlighted the institutional response and management strategies.
   [Interpretive positioning] My lens as a senior clinical nurse emphasizes frontline practices, potentially missing how management decisions influence these practices.
   [Next-round adjustment] I will aim to incorporate management perspectives and responses into future coding to provide a more comprehensive understanding.

coding_output:
Initial Code: Patient fear deters hospital visits  
Clues: "But as soon as they sound the bell that there is a confirmed case in Sierra Leone, the patients in-flow dropped drastically. ... The patients were scared. They were afraid. They think that when they come to the hospital they will catch the virus."  
Initial Code: Increased responsibilities for health workers  
Clues: "No. In fact as a matter of fact, it increased. ... Because I’ve to see the covid patients, and also do my normal clinical work. Right? So it doubled up."  
Initial Code: Implementation of triage system  
Clues: "But now it became compulsory as soon as you are at the hospital’s gate. You must wear your mask if not we won’t see you as health care workers. ... But now it is instituted by management that all patients should have a triage form where in their vitals will be recorded."  
Initial Code: Reduction of elective surgeries  
Clues: "So only emergency patients were operated on. ... All elective cases were put on hold."  
Initial Code: Overwhelmed by patient referrals  
Clues: "Two district- [retracted] district and [retracted] district have outbreak of covid in their theaters. So they had their theaters shut down. So those patients were been referred to the [retracted] government hospital."  
Initial Code: Change in patient access to surgical services  
Clues: "But now we have revisited those laws again, so now all patients are given equal opportunities for surgical operations."  
Initial Code: Fear of infection affects health worker behavior  
Clues: "It just made me to be very cautious and be with patients. Never trust anyone. Right? Always adhere to your fine principles."  
Initial Code: Shortage of personal protective equipment (PPE)  
Clues: "Because the way and manner in…..how the virus was being, and the lack of IPC gears at that point in time. ... There were few masks, few of the gowns to be used."  
Initial Code: Changes in infection control measures  
Clues: "When I came here it was not….. people were bypassing the triage system. Right? But now it is instituted by management that all patients should have a triage form where in their vitals will be recorded and also other signs and symptoms will be recorded."  
Initial Code: Staffing changes for COVID-19 response  
Clues: "Those that were assigned to see covid patients, most of them were stopped from seeing none covid patients."  
Initial Code: Staffing challenges due to reallocation  
Clues: "The more the better, but the less the more difficult work will be. So definitely those that were left in the department will face huge challenge of work." "Nurses that were trained on managing covid-19 patients, were withdrawn from seen none covid patients." "Yes there were trainings, especially in the line of covid-19."  
Initial Code: Increased stress and anxiety among staff  
Clues: "Everyone was stressed with the covi-19." "So you want to know about this corona virus, how to protect yourself and loved ones, and patients." "The earlier phase of learning you will be enjoying it, but as time goes on you will be bored."  
Initial Code: Fear of infection impacting health worker behavior  
Clues: "For me, I was afraid. I was scared." "Because you don’t have your proper gears to use." "Everyone was afraid if that person doesn’t have a masks and gloves to wear before touching a patient."  
Initial Code: Need for adequate personal protective equipment (PPE)  
Clues: "I won’t work. Because I’m afraid." "Later on the government then intervened and sent those IPCs- gloves, masks, the N95s." "There should be enough IPC material available for health care workers."  
Initial Code: Decreased patient flow due to the COVID-19 outbreak  
Clues: "the patients flow decreased." "When the outbreak started, there were minimal patients that we saw at the department." "Then there was this hold-up on elective cases, handling only emergencies."  
Initial Code: Training initiatives for handling COVID-19  
Clues: "They were like trained on how to take care of covid patients." "We were being trained on how to handle suspected cases and also confirmed cases." "Staffs were being trained in each department on how to manage covid-19 cases."
